Rashi on Pesachim 86a:10:1.hebrew: דתנן שתי אמות - קני מדה היו בשושן הבירה, והוא בית הבנוי על גובה השער, כדתנן במסכת מדות (ע"א מ"ג): שער המזרחי, ועליו שושן הבירה צורה מצויירת. ומפרשינן במנחות: כדי שידעו מהיכן באו. ולהכי הוא דקדשי גגין — לכל דדמין לשתי אמות, דלא הוי צורך המזבח — אבל למילתא אחריתי לא קדשו:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:10:1.english: As we learned: two cubits - [These were] measuring rods that were in Shushan the Capital, which is a chamber built atop the height of the gate, as we learned in Tractate Middot (1:3): "The Eastern Gate, and upon it was Shushan the Capital, a depicted image." And we explain in [Tractate] Menachot [that it was placed there] so that they would know from where they came. And it is for this [purpose] that the roofs were sanctified — for anything similar to the two cubits, which are not needed for the altar — but for any other matter they were not sanctified.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:11:1.english: And why were there one large and one small - Let [the cubit] of Moses suffice for them.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:11:2.hebrew: שיהו אומנין - ששכרן לבנות כך וכך אמות, נוטלין למדת הקטנה של משה ומחזירין הבנין לגזברין למדה האחת מאלו הגדולות, כדי שיוותרו משלהן להקדש ולא בצמצום, שמא יהנו מן ההקדש בחנם ויבואו לידי מעילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:11:2.english: So that the artisans - whom they hired to build so-and-so many cubits, take [their wages] according to the small measure of Moses and return the construction to the treasurers according to one of these large [measures], so that they yield [some] of their own to the consecrated [property] and not [measure] with exactness, lest they benefit from consecrated [property] for nothing and come to misuse of consecrated property.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:11:3.hebrew: ותרתי - גדולות למה לי? תיסגי בשל משה ובחדא מהנך:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:11:3.english: And two - large [cubits], why do I [need them]? It would suffice with that of Moses and with one of those.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:11:4.hebrew: חדא לדהבא וכספא - בזו שאין יתירה על של משה אלא חצי אצבע, היו לאומנות זהב וכסף, כמין טבלאות ושולחנות שהן אומנות כבידה. ובזו שיתירה עליהן אצבע, היו מחזירין בנין אבנים ומוסיפין על תנאן אצבע לכל אמה:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:11:4.english: One for gold and silver - With this [cubit], which is only half a fingerbreadth larger than [that] of Moses, they would [measure] for gold and silver craftsmanship, such as tablets and tables, which are costly work. And with this [cubit], which is a fingerbreadth larger than them, they would return stone construction, adding a fingerbreadth for each cubit to their stipulated [measure].

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:12:1.hebrew: עובי החומה - אלמא ראש החומה נתקדש, דדמו לגגין ועליות:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:12:1.english: The thickness of the wall - Apparently, the top of the wall was sanctified, [even though] they are similar to roofs and upper stories.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:13:1.hebrew: בר שורא - חומה קטנה לפנים מן החומה גדולה, והיא נמוכה ושוה לקרקע גובה העזרה, שקרקע העזרה הולך וגבוה ועולה במעלות:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:13:1.english: Bar shura - A small wall inside the large wall, and it is low and level with the ground [at] the height of the courtyard, for the ground of the courtyard rises higher and higher and ascends by steps.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:14:1.english: Two groups that were eating - one Paschal lamb in one house.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:14:2.hebrew: אלו הופכין פניהן אילך - אינן צריכין להסב אלו כנגד אלו להיות נראין כחבורה אחת, אלא רשאין להפוך פניהם אלו אילך ואלו אילך. ואפילו נראין כשתי חבורות, לא איכפת לן, כדיליף בגמרא שהפסח נאכל אף בשתי בתים לשתי חבורות:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:14:2.english: These turn their faces this way - They do not need to recline facing one another so as to appear as one group; rather, they are permitted to turn their faces, these this way and these that way. And even if they appear as two groups, we do not mind, as [the Gemara] derives that the Paschal lamb may be eaten even in two houses by two groups.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:14:3.hebrew: והמיחם - שמחממין בו חמין שמוזגין בו היין, רשאין לתת באמצע, כדי שיהא נוח לשמש המשמש לשתיהן למזוג משם לכאן ולכאן, ואין צריכין לשנות משאר מנהג כל השנה. ואף על פי שמפסיק בין החבורות, לא איכפת לן. וכשהשמש משמש לשתיהן עומד מחבורה אחת, שהתחיל לאכול עמה מן הפסח, למזוג לחבורה האחרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:14:3.english: And the boiler - [that] in which they heat hot water with which they dilute the wine, they are permitted to place [it] in the middle so that it will be convenient for the attendant who serves both [groups] to pour from there to here and to there, and they do not need to deviate from the usual custom of the rest of the year. And even though it intervenes between the groups, we are not concerned. And when the attendant serves both [groups], he gets up from one group, with which he began to eat of the Paschal lamb, to pour for the other group.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:14:4.hebrew: קופץ את פיו ומחזיר את פניו - לצד חבורתו, שלא יחשדוהו שאוכל עם חבורה האחרת. דסבירא ליה לתנא דידן: הפסח נאכל בשתי חבורות, אבל אדם אחד אינו אוכל בשני מקומות ממנו. ולהכי מוקי "בבית אחד יאכל", שאין אדם אחד אוכל בשני בתים, ושתי חבורות ההופכות פניהן כשתי בתים דמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:14:4.english: He closes his mouth and turns his face - Toward his [own] group, so that [people] will not suspect him of eating with the other group. For our Tanna holds [that] the Paschal lamb may be eaten by two groups, but one person may not eat from it in two places. And therefore he establishes [the verse] "In one house shall it be eaten" [to mean] that one person may not eat in two houses, and two groups that turn their faces [away from each other] are like two houses.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:14:5.hebrew: והכלה - שהיא בושה, רשאה להפוך פניה לצד אחר ולאכול, כדאמרן, פסח נאכל בשתי חבורות:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:14:5.english: And the bride - [Because] she is bashful, she is permitted to turn her face to another side and eat, as we said, [since] a Paschal lamb may be eaten in two groups.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:15:1.hebrew: על הבתים אשר יאכלו אותו - משמע שני בני אדם אוכלין פסח אחד בשתי בתים, דכתיב: "יאכלו" — שנים, "אותו" — חד פסח, "בתים" — שנים:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:15:1.english: Upon the houses wherein they shall eat it - [This] implies [that] two people eat one Paschal lamb in two houses, as it is written: "they shall eat" — two [people]; "it" — one Paschal lamb; "houses" — two [houses].

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:15:2.hebrew: יכול יהא - אדם אחד אוכל בשני מקומות, כגון בשני חדרים או בשתי חבורות ההופכות פניהם. ת"ל: בבית אחד יאכל. ור' יהודה סבר יש אם למסורת כדלקמן: יאכל כתיב, משמע אדם אחד אוכלו בבית א' ולא בשני בתים; אבל גבי אוכלים הרבה, כתיב בתים הרבה:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:15:2.english: I might [have thought] - [that] one person may eat in two places, such as in two rooms or in two groups that turn their faces [away from each other]. The verse states: "In one house shall it be eaten" (ye'akhel). And Rabbi Yehuda holds that the traditional written text (masoret) is authoritative, as [stated] below: it is written yokhal ("he shall eat"), which implies [that] one person eats it in one house and not in two houses; whereas regarding many eaters, it is written "houses" — [meaning] many [houses].

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:16:1.hebrew: השמש - שהיה צולהו, ושכח והכניס כזית לתוך פיו, והוא היה נמנה עליו:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:16:1.english: The attendant - Who was roasting it [the Paschal lamb], and forgot and put an olive-bulk into his mouth, and he was registered for it.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:16:2.english: If he is prudent, he fills his stomach with it - For if he gets up from there, he will no longer eat [of it].

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:17:1.hebrew: מלמד שהאוכל אוכל בשני מקומות - ויאכלו דכתיב בקרא, אכל חד וחד מאוכלין קאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:17:1.english: Teaches that one who eats may eat in two places - And [the word] “they shall eat” that is written in the verse refers to each and every one of those who eat.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:1:1.english: What, is it not [the case] that they eat it on the roofs - Evidently, the roofs of Jerusalem were sanctified.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:2:1.hebrew: אין מפטירין - כשהגיע זמנו להפטר מן הסעודה, דהיינו אחר הפסח שהוא נאכל באחרונה על השבע, שכן חובת כל הקרבנות — כדקיימא לן (חולין דף קלב:) למשחה, לגדולה, כדרך שהמלכים אוכלין — אין נפטרין על ידי אפיקומן:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:2:1.english: We do not conclude - When its time has arrived to depart from the meal — that is, after the Paschal lamb, which is eaten last, upon satiety, for such is the obligation of all offerings, as we hold (Chullin 132b) [that] "lemoshchah" [means] for greatness, in the manner that kings eat — they do not depart by means of afikoman.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:2:2.hebrew: ואמר רב - אפיקומן לשון הוציאו כליכם מכאן, ונלך ונאכל עוד בחבורה אחרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:2:2.english: And Rav said - Afikoman [is] an expression [meaning], "Take out your utensils from here, and let us go and eat more in another group."

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:2:3.english: Not during the time of eating - [This refers to] the recitation of Hallel after eating.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:3:1.hebrew: פעם אחת בשנה - ביוה"כ, לקטורת ולהזיית בין הבדים:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:3:1.english: Once a year - On Yom Kippur, for the incense and for the sprinkling [of the blood] between the staves [of the ark].

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:3:2.english: In a week [of years] - In a Sabbatical [cycle].

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:3:3.hebrew: מה היא צריכה - שמא תבקע החומה וצריכה תיקון. אלמא עליות נתקדשו:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:3:3.english: What it needs - Lest the wall crack and it needs repair. Thus, upper stories were sanctified.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:4:1.hebrew: שאני היכל - דכתיב ביה ועליותיו, וכתיב הכל בכתב מיד ה' עלי השכיל, אלמא קדוש:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:4:1.english: The Sanctuary is different - For it is written regarding it, "and of its upper rooms," and it is written, "All this is put in writing by the hand of the Lord, Who has instructed me" — thus [it is] consecrated.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:5:1.english: In the sanctified [area] - In the [Temple] courtyard.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:5:2.english: And open to the unsanctified [area] - For they do not have an entrance to the courtyard, rather to the Temple Mount.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:5:3.hebrew: תוכן חול - כקדושת הר הבית, ולא כעזרה, דבתר פתיחה אזיל:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:5:3.english: Their interiors are unsanctified - Like the sanctity of the Temple Mount, and not like [that of] the Courtyard, for it follows the opening.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:5:4.hebrew: בשגגותיהן שוין לקרקע עזרה - שהלשכות בנויות מחילות תחת הקרקע, הלכך גגים דידהו הוו להו כי ארעא:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:5:4.english: When their roofs are level with the ground of the courtyard - For the chambers are built [as] cavities beneath the ground; therefore, their roofs are like the ground.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:6:1.hebrew: כי אמרה רבי יוחנן - להא דמחילות לא נתקדשו — בפתוחות להר הבית. דגבי שילוח בעל קרי המשתלח חוץ להר הבית אמרה, באלו דברים, דקאמר: מחילות לא נתקדשו, ובעל קרי משתלח חוץ לשתי מחנות, ומותר ליכנס במחילות דהר הבית:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:6:1.english: When Rabbi Yoḥanan said it - [regarding] this [statement] that tunnels were not sanctified, [he was referring] to [tunnels] open to the Temple Mount. For he said it regarding the sending out of a ba'al keri [one who experienced a seminal emission], who is sent outside the Temple Mount, in [the chapter] Eilu Devarim, where he states: tunnels were not sanctified, and a ba'al keri is sent outside two camps, and [nevertheless] it is permitted [for him] to enter the tunnels of the Temple Mount.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:6:2.hebrew: כי תניא ההיא - דתוכן קודש, בפתוחות לעזרה. להכי נקט פתוחות, דבתר פתיחתן אזלינן:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:6:2.english: When that [baraita] was taught - [stating] that their interiors are sanctified, [it refers] to [chambers] open to the courtyard. For this reason it stated "open," because we follow [the location of] their opening.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:7:1.hebrew: והתניא מחילות שתחת היכל חול - וקא סלקא דעתך בפתוחות לעזרה קאמר, ומשנינן: בפתוחות לחול, שמחילות מהלכות מתחת אחת עשרה אמה שאחורי בית הכפורת עד שנפתחות להר הבית מחוץ לעזרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:7:1.english: But wasn't it taught: The tunnels under the Sanctuary are unsanctified - And it was initially assumed [that Rabbi Yehuda] is speaking of [tunnels] that open into the Courtyard, and we answer: [He is speaking] of [tunnels] that open to the unsanctified [area], for tunnels run beneath the eleven cubits behind the Chamber of the Ark-cover [the Holy of Holies] until they open onto the Temple Mount outside the Courtyard.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:8:1.hebrew: ת"ש וגגו קודש - גגו של היכל, וסיפא דהא דרבי יהודה היא. והכא לא מצי לשנויי כדלעיל "מהיכל ניתיב איניש", דהא גגו לא כתיב בקרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:8:1.english: Come [and] hear: And its roof is sacred - [This refers to] the roof of the Sanctuary, and it is the latter clause of that [baraita] of Rabbi Yehuda. And here one cannot answer as above, "From the Sanctuary, should a person sit?" — for its roof is not written in the verse.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:9:1.english: These roofs - [That are] in the [Temple] Courtyard and its chambers.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:9:2.hebrew: אין אוכלין שם קדשי קדשים - הנאכלין בעזרה, ואין שוחטין שם קדשים קלים הנשחטין בכל מקום בעזרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:9:2.english: One may not eat offerings of the most sacred order there - which are eaten in the [Temple] courtyard, and one may not slaughter offerings of lesser sanctity there, which are slaughtered anywhere in the [Temple] courtyard.

Rashi on Pesachim 86a:9:3.hebrew: לאותן שתי אמות - להכי קדשי גגין, לשימוש נתינת כלי קודש הצריכין לבנין, אבל לא הצריכין למזבח, כדאשכחן שאותן שתי אמות — מקלות של מדה — היו נתונות בגובה השער, שהוא בגגין ובעליות:
Rashi on Pesachim 86a:9:3.english: For those two cubits - For this [purpose] roofs are sanctified: for the use of placing sacred vessels that are needed for building, but not those needed for the altar, as we find that those two cubits — measuring sticks — were placed at the top of the gate, which is among the roofs and upper chambers.

Tosafot on Pesachim 86a:14:1.hebrew: הכלה הופכת פניה - איצטריך לאשמעינן דלא חשבינן כשתי מקומות, אע"פ שאכלה מקצת סעודה בלא הפיכת פניה; אי נמי, קמ"ל דחייבת להפוך פניה, כדאמר בגמרא: "כלה" תנן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 86a:14:1.english: The bride turns her face - [This] was necessary to teach us that we do not consider [it] as two [separate] places, even though she ate part of [the] meal without turning her face; alternatively, it teaches us that she is obligated to turn her face, as the Gemara says: "We learned 'a bride.'"

Tosafot on Pesachim 86a:9:1.hebrew: לא נצרכה אלא לאותן שתי אמות - לא בעי למימר דאותן שתי אמות היו מונחות בגגו של היכל, דהא שער מזרחי שעליו שושן הבירה צורה אחת משערי העזרה היה, אלא ה"ק: כמו שאותו שער מזרחי היה מקודש להניח שם כלי קודש, כמו כן "גגו של היכל קודש" דקאמר — היינו להצניע שם כלי קודש; ולא שיהיו כלי קודש צריכין מקום מקודש, כדמוכח בכמה דוכתי, אלא הך קדושה אית להו להניחם שם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 86a:9:1.english: "It was needed only for those two cubits" - It does not mean to say that those two [measuring] cubits were placed on the roof of the Sanctuary, for the Eastern Gate, upon which [there was] a figure of Shushan HaBirah, was one of the gates of the Courtyard. Rather, this is what it is saying: just as that Eastern Gate was sanctified to place sacred vessels there, so too, [when the Gemara] says "the roof of the Sanctuary is sacred," that means to store sacred vessels there. And [it is] not that sacred vessels require a sanctified place, as is proven in several places; rather, they [the roof and the gate] have this [degree of] sanctity, [namely] to place them there.
